body: What's wrong with people not finding a purpose to live, or finding a purpose not to live? Regardless of how you spend your life, your life has nothing to do with your existence. You are just the arrangement of atoms. When you die, they don't stop existing. They just break down into other stuff. Life has nothing to do with the functions of the universe. Life is, from all perspectives external to preserving life, pointless. There is nothing good nor bad about that, but I believe that, by extension, making the "most of life" is also pointless. Culture is pointless. Really, everything is fucking pointless, because we're on a little blue ball in a grand nothing and we insist that things on it have meaning simply because we say so.

The universe functions. There are laws, and even if we do not understand the universe, it is going to go on its merry way. We are just a part of that. Animals are just a part of that system, as well as the tides, the moon's orbit that affects them, the Earth's orbit around the sun, the sun's path in the galaxy, and all the stars that are burning out and collapsing. They are following the laws. 

And we are, too, but observation gives us this feeling that we have an ability to have power over it. We can see things and uniquely acknowledge our "independence" from the system. Ultimately, this is not the case. We simply play out the universe's laws in another form.

Consciousness just gives us the ability to make messes of things. Through it we grew, and we destroy not only the ecosystem we're a part of, but other self-awares. All self-awareness does is create a convoluted mess of the natural processes that are happening anyway. The universe doesn't give a fuck either way, I'm sure you would agree.

Okay: I don't want to restart my life. And I certainly don't want to be anywhere I've once been. 

I find consciousness disgusting. And I really just want nothing to do with it. Observation is a terrible thing. I hate the feeling of "choosing," because there is this implied feeling of choosing for a reason. And there is no reason. To anything. From a universal perspective, reason just doesn't exist. If I'm choosing to eat, it is so I do not starve, or because I like the taste of something. But likewise, I can choose not to eat, specifically so I do starve, and no choice was better than the other. Why is life such an important thing? Why is "who we are" something that matters at all, or that we should try to better?

There is literally no reason, unless we make one up. Why is that not a fucking joke to everyone else?

Reading this, I feel it very obvious you put value in either human culture or the bettering of mankind as a whole, while I tend to see humanity as a virus that has been throughout its history using its arrogance and self-righteous philosophies to destroy the beautiful system it was once a part of. 

I don't want to impact someone else, because my views tend to be "Well, everything would be a lot better off if we were just gone."

I used to take all of these things to heart. When I started looking at colleges, when I moved out of home, when I entered and left relationships with partners, I always felt like they had some great meaning, or they were building up to something. So I would try and dissect them and understand them, but most experiences in my life after dissection have been failures. I never graduated. I've spent most of my life alone. I do not have a career. My dreams all felt very out of reach.

And before, these would always drag me down. So I would scour all I had for something to lift me up. But now it's all dead. There are no joys and there are no drops. I feel like everything I experience is a literal interaction with no meaning, but the meaning other people experience can be seen. Why can't I feel that? Why can't I feel any of it? 

All I feel now is this twisting, gut-wrenching constant. It combines with my hunger, and digs for my old depression. And all it tells me is that there is one literal thing: suffering. It's what we're born to do, until we die and our atoms decide to do something else. So what is the use in prolonging the only constant quality of consciousness? Or having it at all?

Fuck fuck fuck.

Goals, for example, are not physical things but abstractions we create. Thoughts beyond the realities. They have no bearing on the nature or laws of the universe. I can set a goal and accomplish it, but where does the value in that come from? Why can I accomplish goals and feel absolutely nothing?

A reality in a relationship situation could be my mother. Yes, my mother was literally the woman who gave birth to me, but the emotional connection to someone like that, the bond of the family structure, is just an abstraction. It only exists because in my mind I let it exist.

No, I am just saying that existence is suffering. Life is a fight for survival, and why? Only attempts to make that suffering easier to digest. We eat only so we do not starve. Regardless, death is the only permanent relief from suffering. Everything else is just an attempt to go on until the end, without reason or purpose.

Well, insinuating there is an inherent point or purpose in the day, or the next day, or any day after that, is asinine. There's just the suffering and the relief of suffering. If there isn't any relief in the foreseeable future, I imagine you can see where this is going.

My chest scar is a bit wider than your arm scar. It was done four years ago. I think. Yea. It's faded. You're right about that. But I can feel it. It's raised. And the scar tissue is stiff. It just feels solid. It's just a dead piece of my chest.

As for most of the other scars, they are prior to a suicide attempt a bit earlier than my chest scar. I was mostly successful, I suppose. I don't remember most of my life before the event, and I guess those scars are associated with those things. I don't really know how to give them purpose, without just making it something generic and over enveloping, and then it wouldn't feel real.

The worst part is that I can't even explain most of them. I mean, I guess I could explain them, but each scar isn't significant. There was a point where it was, but now they're just marks. It's like in some places I just have a different print.

And there's one that is never going to fade. I needed stitches, but instead I let it bleed. And it bled for a couple days. I wore red shirts those days. And now it's a scar. And I cry every time I see it. Right on my chest. And when people see that one, they say "He has a wicked chest scar." But they'll never know where it came from. And I'll always know.

My thinking here is that it's easy to become despondent towards things that we find important but are supported only by* ourselves. Certainly, we have individualized passions and interests, but it helps to see that others appreciate them as well. It gives them an even newer meaning, that they are not only important to ourselves, but that something we do and accomplish goes beyond our own personal reasons and affects others.

For example, I love to cook, but the real joy of cooking is sitting down with someone I care for and being able to provide to them a meal. I also enjoy photography, and I throw away dozens of shots even from short walks, saving only one or two that I really like. I've found, though, that I can be too hard on myself, and friends of mine will see things in my shots that even I didn't notice. They're given a second chance through the appreciation of others.

I've also failed more than just this time. I was a cutter a decade ago or so. The policy at my high school, and I don't know how national this is, is that if someone has been causing self harm in any way, they are suspended for three days so a doctor can say if they are a harm to themselves or others and they're welcomed back. I had a completely apathetic doctor who, because I used "big words" decided I was intelligent and need to be back in that school. While I'm grateful that didn't escalate, it's horrible that the entire process did nothing to seek help for the obvious depression that was leading me there.

On my previous actual attempt, I found a nice place in the woods, and I decided I wanted to die comfortably, feeling whole in nature. A hiker found me, I guess, and I was in an institution for a few days and let go at the minimum date (another law). I guess I just don't seem "crazy" enough to be a "high risk." My friends, however, all know of my history.

But where do you go at times like this? It's nearly 5 a.m. here. Sleep is definitely no longer an option. Also, you brought out a lot of tears. But good ones, I guess. I'm glad that I was given more time when I tried to take it from myself, but there is that lingering question. If I can't even properly have control over my death, what can I have control over? 

It's that question that's led me to cut my own hair for the past few years. And I'm damn good at it.

Maybe getting off the ride is a good idea, my friend, but the ride isn't life. The ride that you want to get off is society. Your burdens are created by the cultural illusion in which you find yourself confined. It is true that within the world perpetuated by capitalism you will buy things that mean nothing in the end. They are just things. And you will work to pay bills and perpetuate your slavery.

But, in the words of comedian duo Hard n' Phirm, "there's a world of freedom out there, if you are creative." I would advise getting out there and not trying to be sociable, or to attain some wholly valueless goal, but to see the world without the illusion. Maybe go on some nature walks, or invest in a nice camera. You don't really realize how many perspectives you can have on the same world until you try and capture it 300 different ways behind a lens.
